subject: Life Sciences
topicAf: DNS: die kode van die lewe

items.q: Chargaff showed that %A = %T and %G = %C in DNA. Which base pairs with cytosine?
items.qAf: Chargaff het getoon dat %A = %T en %G = %C in DNS. Watter basis paar met sitosien?
items.explain: In DNA, guanine pairs with cytosine by three hydrogen bonds.
items.explainAf: In DNS paar guanien met sitosien deur drie waterstofbindings.

items.q: A DNA molecule has 20% adenine. What percentage is guanine?
items.qAf: ’n DNS-molekule het 20% adenien. Watter persentasie is guanien?
items.explainAf: A = T = 20%, dus is G + C = 60% en G = C = 30%.

items.q: Which of these is NOT found in DNA?
items.qAf: Watter een hiervan kom NIE in DNS voor nie?
items.explain: Uracil is found in RNA, not DNA; DNA uses thymine instead.
items.explainAf: Urasiel kom in RNA voor, nie in DNS nie; DNS gebruik timien in plaas daarvan.

items.explain: The DNA is transcribed into mRNA in the nucleus.
items.explainAf: Die DNS word in die kern na mRNA getranskribeer.

items.q: An mRNA codon reads AUG. Which amino acid does it code for?
items.qAf: ’n mRNA-kodon lees AUG. Watter aminosuur kodeer dit?
items.explain: AUG is the start codon and codes for methionine.
items.explainAf: AUG is die beginkodon en kodeer vir metionien.

items.q: A single base is deleted from the coding sequence of a gene. What is the most likely effect?
items.qAf: ’n Enkele basis word uit die kodeervolgorde van ’n geen uitgevee. Wat is die waarskynlikste effek?
options: A frameshift mutation that changes all amino acids after the deletion
Only the mRNA changes, not the protein
optionsAf: A frameshift mutation that changes all amino acids after the deletion
Only the mRNA changes, not the protein
items.explain: Deleting one base shifts the reading frame, changing every codon after the deletion.
items.explainAf: Die uitvee van een basis skuif die leesraamwerk, wat elke kodon na die uitvee verander.
